newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia oilmen unable to pump out Coporo crude.
newsitem.headline: Colombia oilmen unable to pump out Coporo crude.

text.p: One of the biggest oil fields in Colombia, a country already known for its difficult drilling conditions, looks set be the hardest yet to exploit, sources at state oil company Ecopetrol said Tuesday.
An 18,000-foot deep (5,500 meter) test well has recently been completed at a cost of $50 million in the Coporo field in Colombia's eastern plains.

But dense rock formations, coupled with the virtual absence of natural gas or water, which would normally help force crude to the surface, means that extracting estimated reserves of as much as 2 billion barrels will be extremely difficult.
"This a very great difficulty. We're consulting technicians across the world looking for a method which would allow us to get at the oil," an Ecopetrol spokesman told Reuters.
"We must overcome this problem. It would be ridiculous to just sit on such a huge field but obviously this problem will push up eventual production costs," he added.
Ecopetrol is considering the possibility of drilling for water nearby and reinjecting it to force oil to the surface.
Alternatively, one of the multinationals operating in Colombia may be provide a solution, he said.
Under a clause in Ecopetrol's association contracts, foreign companies are obliged to transfer new technology to the Colombian state oil industry when required.
During a visit to New York in September President Ernesto Samper said Coporo contained at least 700 million barrels in one level alone.

Geologists believe the field may contain a total of between 1.5 billion and 2 billion barrels, although Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar has said this is not necessarily a commercial figure.
